_notes: Concept prompts for the built things: stations and chests, which LocalSpawn makes whole (Hunyuan3D shape + UltraTex
texture), and buildings, which are built in Blender from the building kit after their concept image (an asset with
'kit': its script; only its concept image is generated here).
Same phases and keys as gathering_manifest.json (generate_gathering.py --group structures); the models go to the
'art' folder and into the prefabs by AgentScripts/BuildStructureModels.cs.
Fires are made cold (no flames, no glow, no smoke): the game adds the flame, the light and the sparks.
Sod roofs are drawn bare (dark peat, no grass): the game grows its own grass on the roof.
A building is made to look like its concept image, not like the stand-in it replaces: one long low building seen
from its open or entrance side, which is the side the game's camera looks at.
UltraTex (FLUX) is a non-commercial licence and Hunyuan3D's licence excludes some territories: re-texture/check before a release.

2026-11-14, the user: replace the remaining primitive stand-ins with LocalSpawn models (Kitchen to Farm Bed). Their flames, glows and lights stay in the game's prefabs (BuildStructureModels.Placeholders).
2026-11-22, the user: "cauldron needs a proper 3D model" (it was a borrowed table with three spheres). Its brew's glow stays in the prefab.
common: Three-quarter view from slightly above, whole object visible and centred, isolated on a plain light grey background. Matte, softly lit, no glow.

looks.prompt: A cold unlit campfire: a ring of nine rounded grey field stones, each the size of a loaf of bread, set close together around a bed of pale grey ash and black charcoal, with five short split birch logs, white bark and charred black ends, laid low in a star across the middle. No flames, no smoke, no embers.

A sturdy old Norse wooden sea chest, closed, with a slightly curved lid, thick weathered oak planks, three hammered black iron straps with round rivets running over the lid and down the front, an iron hasp with a ring lock in the middle of the front, and an iron carrying ring on each end.

A small old Norse village smithy, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a squat chimney of grey stones with a flat cap stone rising through the roof at one end; the long front side open under the eave between two timber posts with diagonal braces, showing a stone forge inside, with an iron anvil on a tree stump and a wooden quench barrel standing at the opening. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village workshop, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; the long front side open under the eave between timber posts with diagonal braces, showing a carpenter's and stonemason's workshop inside: a heavy wooden workbench with a vice and tools on it, a rack of saws, hammers and chisels on the back wall, a round grindstone in a wooden frame, a sawhorse with a plank across it, and a half-carved block of grey stone standing at the opening. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village woodcutter's lodge, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a closed log cabin at the left end with a plank door, and to the right of it the long front side open under the eave between timber posts, sheltering a long sawbench with a big two-handed frame saw; a tall stack of round logs and a neat stack of sawn planks beside the opening, a chopping block with an axe standing in it, and two round wooden shields leaning against the wall. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village hunter's lodge, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a plank door in the middle of the long front side with a pair of antlers above it, and a small shuttered window; beside the door a wooden frame with a brown animal hide stretched and laced on it, a rack of poles with strips of meat and fish hung to dry, a bow and a quiver hanging on the wall, and a chopping stump. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village weaver's and tailor's house, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a plank door at the left end of the long front side and, along the rest of it, an open porch under the eave between timber posts, with an upright wooden weaving loom with stone weights, baskets of grey wool, a low bench, and a line of dyed cloth in dull red, blue and ochre hung up to dry. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village trading post, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; the long front side open under the eave between timber posts, with a long plank counter across the opening; behind and beside it crates, barrels and bulging sacks, a hanging balance scale, furs and a coil of rope hung from the posts, and a striped cloth awning stretched out over the counter on two poles. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village family cottage, one low building seen from outside, a little wider than it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a plank door with iron hinges in the middle of the long front side under a small porch roof on two posts, a small window with wooden shutters, a squat chimney of grey stones with a flat cap stone rising through the roof; a bench beside the door and a neat stack of split firewood against the wall. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A very small old Norse village sleeping hut, one low building seen from outside, a little wider than it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a low plank door in the long front side and no window; a bench made of a split log beside the door and a wooden bucket. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse village bathhouse, a log sauna, one low building seen from outside, a little wider than it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a low plank door in the long front side, a stubby chimney of grey stones rising through the roof; a bench beside the door with a wooden bucket and a bundle of leafy birch twigs on it, and a water barrel at the corner. No people, no fire, no smoke.

A small old Norse wooden jetty at a lake shore, seen from outside: a narrow deck of weathered grey-brown oak planks laid across two long log beams, standing on thick round log posts driven into the ground, about four metres long and two wide, with a low rail on one side. On the deck a wooden fish-drying rack of two posts and a pole with a fishing net hung over it, a coil of thick rope, a small wooden barrel, and at the far end a tall post with an iron lantern hanging from an arm. No water, no boat, no people.

A small old Norse village stable, one long low building about three times as wide as it is tall, seen from outside: a back wall and two end walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark under the roof's edges; the whole long front side open under the eave, held by four timber posts with diagonal braces, divided inside into four stalls by low log partitions, each stall with a wooden hay rack on the back wall full of golden hay and a log water trough, straw on the floor. No horses, no people.

A small old Norse cartwright's workshop yard, seen from outside: a low open timber shelter on four posts with diagonal braces under a low-pitched roof of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass and no plants, a peeled log along each eave; under it a heavy wooden workbench with tools; around it a half-built wooden cart frame standing on two trestles, two big spoked wooden cart wheels with iron tyres leaning against a post, a stack of planks, a chopping block with an axe, and a wooden tub. No people.

An old Norse outdoor cooking hearth: a waist-high block of fitted grey field stones with a flat slab top, a short square stone chimney rising from its left end, a round black iron cooking pot set into the top on the right, and a thick plank work board along the front with two wooden bowls and a ladle. Cold: no fire, no smoke.

An old Norse village well: a round knee-high wall of fitted grey field stones around a dark opening, two stout wooden posts on either side holding a wooden windlass with coiled rope, a wooden bucket resting on the stone rim, and a small pitched roof of wooden shingles on top of the posts.

A small old Norse wooden lookout tower: four tall rough log posts with diagonal cross-braces, a square plank platform at the top with a low log railing, a simple log ladder leaning against one side, and a small iron lantern hanging from one corner post. Unlit.

A small old Norse open-fronted storage lean-to: a sloping roof of wooden shingles on four stout posts, the back and sides walled with horizontal planks, open at the front, with grain sacks, two barrels and a wooden crate stacked inside on a floor of flat stones.

A Viking age iron smelting furnace: a squat round tower of grey field stones and cracked brown clay about chest high, narrowing to a short chimney, a small arched opening at the bottom front, and a pair of leather bellows on a low wooden frame beside it. Cold: no fire, no glow, no smoke.

An ancient Norse stone altar: a low square plinth of fitted grey stones, on top a round carved stone basin with a shallow bowl, pale green runes cut into its sides, a little moss in the cracks. The basin is empty. Matte runes.

A tall Viking age standing torch: a straight rough wooden pole set upright in a small mound of fist-sized grey stones, its top end thickly wrapped in dark brown tarred rags bound round with twine. Unlit: no flame, no smoke, no metal.
A wooden lantern post: a squared timber post about two metres tall with a short arm at its top, and a small iron-framed lantern with pale horn panes hanging from the arm. Unlit.

A tall wooden banner pole with a short crossbar near the top, hanging a long woven wool banner in deep blue with an ochre border and a stitched ochre tree emblem, a carved round wooden knob on top of the pole, its foot set in a few grey stones.
A low rectangular raised planter box of weathered wooden planks, filled to the brim with dark crumbly soil, nothing planted.
A traditional Norse straw bee skep: a dome of coiled straw bands bound with willow, sitting on a small square wooden stand with four short legs, a small entrance hole at the bottom front.

An old Norse ward stone: a tall rough-hewn grey standing stone on a low square stone base, deep pale blue runes carved down its front, and a few feathers and small bones tied to it with cord. Matte runes.
A square patch of dark earth inside a low frame of rough split logs, with nine short thick sharpened wooden stakes pointing up in three neat rows, pale fresh-cut points.
A square patch of dark earth inside a low frame of wooden boards, with nine short sharp black iron spikes pointing up in three neat rows.

A large festival bonfire built and waiting, never lit: a tall cone of split birch logs leaned together, clean white bark, standing on bare earth inside a ring of big rounded grey stones. Cold: no fire, no flames, no glow, no embers, no smoke, no charring.
A straw training dummy: a bundle of straw bound with rope into a rough body and round head, a wooden crossbar through it for arms, on a stout wooden post standing in a small wooden cross foot.
A straw training dummy on a wooden post wearing a battered iron mail shirt and a dented round iron helmet, a wooden crossbar for arms, on a wooden cross foot.
A rectangular farm bed of dark tilled soil in neat furrows, edged with a low frame of split logs. Bare soil, nothing growing yet.

A straight four-metre section of an old Norse defensive palisade seen square from the front: twelve thick upright tree trunks of the same dark weathered grey-brown bark, packed tightly side by side with no gaps, each sharpened to a point at the top, bound together with rope. Nothing sticks out past the first and last trunk. Perfectly straight.

A straight four-metre section of an old dry-stone wall seen square from the front: fitted grey field stones stacked head high without mortar, a little moss in the joints, a flat top, both ends cut off clean and square.

An old Norse brewing station: a round-bellied black iron cauldron with a thick rolled rim and two ring handles, hung by a short iron chain from a tripod of three stout wooden poles lashed together with rope at the top, over a ring of grey field stones with cold grey ash and black charcoal beneath. Bundles of dried herbs and a string of mushrooms hang from one pole, and a low plank bench beside it holds three clay jars, a stone mortar and pestle and a wooden ladle. Cold: no fire, no steam, no smoke, nothing glowing.
